subject: Q2 renewal prep — usage trajectory and upsell recommendation
messages:
From: Samantha Cho <samantha@clearsight.io>
To: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
Cc: account-admin@clearsight.io
Date: Tue, 18 May 2027 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Usage spike ahead of renewal — can we align on terms?

Hi Marcus,

We're lining up our contract renewal with Redwood in early July and wanted to get a compact health/usage review in front of you. Over the last 8 weeks we've seen a ~3x increase in token consumption tied to new LLM-powered features (streaming chat + short-response embeddings). That jump is outpacing our forecast and will materially affect our cost model for Q3.

Can someone from your side share a short ROI recap and a recommended path for smoothing unit costs? Specifically we're interested in:
- A committed throughput/commit tier that would bring per-token price down materially
- Any immediate runtime knobs (batching, KV caching, quantization profiles) we can flip to reduce burn this quarter
- Example term concessions (term length vs discount) you've given other similar customers

I've attached our usage export for Q1->mid Q2 so you can see the surge. Happy to jump on a 30-min call if helpful.

Thanks,
Samantha Cho
Head of ML Ops | Clearsight Analytics
[Attachment: Clearsight_usage_Q1_Q2.csv (csv, 58KB)]
From: Marcus Lin <marcus_lin@redwood.com>
To: Samantha Cho <samantha@clearsight.io>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 19 May 2027 10:07:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Usage spike ahead of renewal — can we align on terms?

Thanks for the data, Samantha — appreciate the heads up.

Quick read: the uplift looks concentrated in two areas: (1) embeddings batch sizes dropped after you moved the pipeline to per-request embeddings, and (2) a spike in streaming token emission in a new recommendation flow. Both are solvable without degrading UX.

I'll loop in Laura (pricing/commit modeling) and Neha (solutions/ops) to draft a concise ROI recap and a few commercially viable options (commit increases, term trade-offs, pilot Dedicated). Can you confirm the renewal target date and whether procurement needs a single PO or an SOW + PO?

Proposed next step: we'll send a short one-pager and a 2-option term sheet by Friday. If that looks good we can schedule a 30-min alignment call next week.

Best,
Marcus Lin
Head of Revenue, Platform | Redwood Inference

Looping in analysis. High-level findings after a quick pass on the CSV Marcus attached:

1) Cost drivers
- Embeddings: average batch size fell from ~48 to ~6 after the frontend change — that multiplies per-embedding overhead.
- Streaming: a new recommend endpoint emits longer tails for some sessions (median +40% tokens).

2) Immediate ops levers (low friction)
- Reintroduce small request batching for embeddings (client-side queueing) — expected ~35-45% token reduction for embedding flows.
- Enable prefix KV caching for the recommend pipeline to avoid re-computing context for repeat tails (~15-25% token savings).
- Apply int8 quantization for the candidate model in the recommend path (no quality degradation observed in our internal A/B tests).

3) Commercial options (what to offer Clearsight)
- Option A (Conservative): 12-month term, +30% commit over last 30d average, 12% unit discount, priority burst capacity.
- Option B (Aggressive): 18-month term, +50% commit, 20% unit discount, pilot Dedicated slot for 90 days to stabilize latency at scale.

4) Financials & ROI
- If Clearsight implements the low-friction ops levers and chooses Option B, estimated net monthly spend (post-discount) should be within 5-10% of current plan while supporting the higher traffic. We put numbers into the attached cost model.

I'll package a short one-pager and a draft proposal PDF. Marcus — I'll need a quick confirmation on allowable discount caps and whether legal prefers an amendment or a new SOW.

Cheers,
Laura Bennett
Senior Strategic Accounts | Redwood Inference
[Attachment: cost_model_v2.xlsx (xlsx, 240KB)]

Thanks, Laura — that's super helpful. A couple of clarifying Qs from my finance/infra teams:

- For Option B, can you share the committed throughput (tokens/sec or concurrent sessions) that maps to the +50% commit? Our SREs want concrete capacity guarantees.
- The Dedicated pilot: what are the uplift SLAs and how would failover to hosted be handled during the pilot (especially for high-traffic windows)?
- For procurement: we need an ROI table showing expected monthly spend vs expected savings assuming we implement the batching + KV cache changes.

We're amenable to an 18-month term but need to see the ROI math to get internal approval. Can you also share any prior examples (anonymized) of customers who reduced unit cost via the runtime levers you suggested?

Best,
Samantha

Samantha — attaching the proposed action plan and draft commercial term sheet (RDW-2384). Highlights:

- Pilot scope: 90-day Dedicated pilot with 99.5% uptime SLA for the Dedicated slot. Failover is handled via automated routing to hosted instances; during failover we offer a 30% capacity-preservation buffer to keep tails graceful.
- Commit mapping: +50% commit maps to a sustained 35k tokens/sec aggregate across Clearsight's tenant (we've sized for your QPS from the attached export). Burst headroom included up to 45k tokens/sec for short windows.
- Financials: Option B (18 months) modeled in the attached proposal — net blended unit price is ~18% below current effective per-token spend given the operational savings. ROI table and assumptions are in the first tab.
- Commercial ask: we'd require a DocuSign signature on the amendment + a 30-day notice for pilot activation so we can provision Dedicated capacity.

Related links:
- HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/contacts/12345/deal/2384
- DocuSign (pre-auth): https://www.docusign.com/recipient?envelopeId=0a1b2c3d4e

If this aligns, I'll open the SOW + amendment with legal and send the DocuSign envelope. Can we aim to finalize by June 11 so we can start pilot provisioning by June 21?

Next steps I propose:
1) Clearsight confirms: procurement flow (PO vs SOW) and an internal sign-off owner.
2) Redwood sends DocuSign + SOW draft.
3) Technical kickoff with Neha's team to scope KV cache and batching changes (we estimate 2 weeks of dev effort to roll changes safely).

Thanks — happy to hop on a call tomorrow if preferred.

Regards,
Marcus Lin
Head of Revenue, Platform | Redwood Inference
